text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The chairman of Lithuania's Christian Democratic Union Kazys Bobelis said on Thursday that he will run in the presidential elections in December.
- Lithuania expects that the agreement between Russia and NATO will not decide its fate.
- Lithuania's finance ministry banned Nomura from guaranteeing government bonds.

- Lithuania's finance minister Algirdas Shemeta told a capital markets conference in Vilnius on Thursday that the governmnet forecasts the country's GDP will grow by five percent this year and eight percent in 1998.
- The board of the Bank of Lithuania decided to revoke the banking license of Innovation Bank from May 26.
- The official opening ceremony of the new residence of the President of Lithuania will be held today.
- Defence attorney Margarita Shalkauskiiene ,36, was sentenced to three and half years in prison for giving a bribe.
- The Lithuanian government wants to increase the deposit insurance sum from 5,000 ECU to 15,000 ECU in two years. Deposits in Lithuania are now insured for 1,000 ECU.
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development forecasts that Lithuania's GDP will grow by no less than four percent in 1997.
- The Lithuanian Investment agency said that country's 20 biggest foreign investors have increased their investments by 70 percent in the past year.

- Pakistan Bhoja Airlines has negotiated with Lithuania's transport ministry to acquire 11 YAK 42 planes from Lithuanian Airlines. The transport minister Alhis Zhvaliauskas said that the deal might be worth 68 million litas.
